subject: Post-incident summary and remediation plan — SummitPay
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Bell <jordan.bell@summitpay.com>; Ashley Quinn <ashley.quinn@summitpay.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 08:13:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary and remediation plan — SummitPay

Jordan / Ashley,

First, thank you for your patience this morning while we investigated the degraded responses you observed across the Redwood inference endpoints for your production org. I want to share a concise customer-facing summary of what happened, what we did to mitigate it, and the next steps we are taking to prevent recurrence.

Summary (high level)
- Incident window: 2026-07-09 14:02:12 UTC — 2026-07-09 15:05:47 UTC.
- Impact: Elevated latency and intermittent 503s for a subset of inference requests routed to a specific dedicated pool serving SummitPay traffic. No successful requests were observed to have altered customer data.
- Root cause (preliminary): A cascading resource reclamation bug in our autoscaler combined with an unexpected large-text workload spike that caused KV cache thrashing and transient OOMs on two GPU nodes.

Immediate mitigations performed
- We removed the affected nodes from rotation and redistributed in-flight traffic to cold-standby capacity at 14:06 UTC.
- Temporarily pinned your route to a more conservative concurrency profile to eliminate cache contention.
- Rolled back a recent autoscaler micro-change to prevent premature reclamation while we completed diagnostics.

What we are delivering to you now
- Attached: concise customer-facing RCA (summitpay_rca.pdf) and a CSV timeline (summitpay_timeline.csv).
- A remediation plan with owners and ETA (below).
- We propose a 30-minute call to walk through the RCA and answer any security or compliance questions. Proposed times: Thu 2026-07-09 17:00 UTC or Fri 2026-07-10 13:00 UTC — let me know which works.

Short-term actions (already underway)
- Disable the autoscaler change that triggered premature node reclamation (owner: Evelyn Hart, ETA: 2026-07-09 EOD UTC).
- Increase cold-standby capacity by +25% for SummitPay for the next 7 days while we validate fixes (owner: Lauren Bishop, ETA: 2026-07-09 18:00 UTC).
- Run an audit of recent model-sequence-length distributions for your routes to surface any anomalous spikes (owner: Marcus Lin, ETA: 2026-07-10).

Planned long-term fixes
- Hardening: Add guardrails to the autoscaler to avoid reclaiming nodes that still have hot KV cache (owner: Infra Team, ETA: 2026-08-10).
- Observability: New events and an alert that surface cache-thrashing behavior and per-node OOM risk (owner: Observability, ETA: 2026-07-23).
- Testing: Add a regression test that simulates cache churn under large-sequence workloads (owner: QA, ETA: 2026-07-30).

We know this incident interrupted important traffic for you. I will join the call and have our infra and security leads available. If you prefer, we can treat this as a formal compliance submission—please indicate whether you need a redacted incident package for audit purposes.

Thanks again,

Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0199

Attachments: [summitpay_rca.pdf (PDF, 4 pages) — customer-facing summary], [summitpay_timeline.csv (CSV) — event-level timeline]

From: Jordan Bell <jordan.bell@summitpay.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ashley Quinn <ashley.quinn@summitpay.com>
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-incident summary and remediation plan — SummitPay

Marcus,

Thanks for the rapid update and for the attachments — I skimmed the timeline. A couple of immediate questions from our security and platform teams:

1) Data exposure: can you confirm whether any customer PII or request payloads were written to logs that are accessible outside our org?
2) Logs/retention: we would like a short-term retention of full request/response logs for our account for 30 days to support internal forensics. Can you confirm you can enable that?
3) What are the short-term guardrails we can add on our side (rate limits, sequence-size caps) to reduce risk while you roll out fixes?

We are open to the Fri 13:00 UTC slot for a call. Please include someone from your security team.

Jordan Bell
VP, Engineering — SummitPay
jordan.bell@summitpay.com

To: Jordan Bell <jordan.bell@summitpay.com>; Ashley Quinn <ashley.quinn@summitpay.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>, SecOps <secops@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 9 Jul 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-incident summary and remediation plan — SummitPay (detailed RCA)

Jordan — following up with the detailed RCA and owners. Below is a longer-form timeline and our concrete next steps. I have attached the customer PDF (summitpay_rca.pdf) and the raw event timeline CSV for your security team.

--- Detailed timeline (condensed) ---
14:01:53 UTC — Routine traffic spike detected on SummitPay route; 95th percentile sequence length increased to 18k tokens (normal baseline ~850 tokens).
14:02:12 UTC — First node reported increased GC/allocator pressure; KV cache eviction rate rose sharply.
14:04:41 UTC — Autoscaler metric crossed reclaim threshold; micro-change in autoscaler triggered immediate node reclamation logic (bug path).
14:05:12 UTC — Two nodes hit transient OOMs and began failing health checks; traffic spiked to remaining nodes, causing additional cache thrash.
14:06:09 UTC — We removed affected nodes from rotation and migrated traffic to cold-standby capacity; error rate fell to baseline by 14:18 UTC.
14:24:00 UTC — Autoscaler rollback completed.
15:05:47 UTC — Post-mitigation verification complete; all routes normal.

Root cause (final)
- A latent bug in autoscaler change set 0.8.3 caused node reclamation to trigger based on a transient metric sample without sufficient hysteresis. Under an unusually large-sequence workload the KV cache eviction amplified memory pressure leading to transient OOMs. The autoscaler reclaim logic had no explicit check for active KV cache residency.

Customer impact and data exposure
- We found no evidence that SummitPay request payloads were written to a location accessible outside your account. All request/response logs remain scoped to your org and internal engineering storage as per our logging policy. SecOps performed an integrity check on the log storage buckets and found no unauthorized reads.

Temporary forensic retention
- We can enable a 30-day elevated retention for your account's request/response logs. This will be provisioned by our support team as an account-level change and will not expose logs to other tenants. To proceed we need a signed request from your side (I can send a short authorization form).

Short-term guardrails you can configure
- Apply an upper bound on sequence length per-request on your client side (recommendation: 5k tokens) — this is a safe control to avoid cache bloat.
- Rate-limit burst concurrency to X requests/sec during known heavy windows (we can propose exact numbers on the call).

Action items and owners
- Autoscaler guard (prevent premature reclamation): Infra (Evelyn Hart) — ETA 2026-07-23 (hotfix in 1 week, full rollout by 2026-08-10).
- Increased cold-standby for SummitPay: Ops (Lauren Bishop) — completed 2026-07-09 17:30 UTC (took effect immediately).
- Log retention enablement for SummitPay (support ticket INC-78942): Support (Marcus Lin) — ETA: 2026-07-09 EOD to provision and confirm.
- Audit package and redacted incident bundle for compliance: SecOps (secops@redwood.ai) — ETA 2026-07-12.

We will also add a postmortem blameless writeup to our Trust Center and share the redacted copy with you when ready.

Please find the attached files and the Drive link below. I will be on the Fri 13:00 UTC call and will invite our SecOps lead.

Drive: https://drive.redwood.com/summitpay/rca-20260709
Support ticket: https://support.redwood.com/ticket/INC-78942

Marcus Lin
Head of Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference

Attachments: summitpay_rca.pdf (4 pages, customer summary); summitpay_timeline.csv (event-level CSV)

Marcus,

Received — thanks for the transparent timeline and the proposed mitigation roadmap. We appreciate the retention offer; please proceed to enable the 30-day elevated retention and send the authorization form. Our security ops contact (security@summitpay.com) will sign.

We will take the recommended client-side caps in the short term and will discuss longer-term controls on the call. Fri 13:00 UTC works for our team — please share a calendar invite with the SecOps contact and your security lead.

Jordan
